name: Jamin
overview: Jamin was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, noted in Scripture as a son of Simeon. He is listed among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking his place in the early history of the Israelite people. His descendants, known as the Jaminites, are mentioned in the census of the tribe of Simeon.
namesAndTitles: The name Jamin means 'right hand' or 'south,' which can be understood as an indication of good fortune. This proper name is recorded in Genesis 46:10 and is not explicitly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jamin as a son of Simeon, establishing his direct lineage within the tribe of Simeon. No other family relationships are detailed beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jamin's significance lies in his role as a progenitor within the tribe of Simeon, one of the tribes of Israel. His inclusion in the list of those who went to Egypt situates him in the foundational narrative of Israel's sojourn in Egypt, a key moment in biblical history. The mention of the Jaminites in the census underscores the continuation of his lineage within the nation of Israel.
